issues.legal_issue: Property acquired by a Hindu female in lieu of maintenance in recognition of a pre-existing right falls within the enlargement of limited ownership into full ownership, notwithstanding restrictions imposed by the instrument or decree granting it.
material_facts: A partition decree required the male holders to pay yearly maintenance to a widow and entitled her, upon default, to take possession of specified land in lieu of maintenance.
After default, the widow obtained possession of the land under the decree, which restricted her power to alienate it.
The widow later transferred part of the land, and the transfer was challenged as void.
issues.conclusion: The property acquired in lieu of maintenance was within Section 14(1) and its Explanation; Section 14(2) did not exclude it from the enlargement of her limited interest into full ownership.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14(1) and 14(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, read with the Explanation to Section 14(1), require a broad construction of the main provision and a construction of the exception that does not defeat its social purpose. Property acquired in lieu of maintenance is expressly included in the Explanation, and where it recognizes a pre-existing right, Section 14(2) does not apply. The Court followed V. Tulasamma v. V. Sesha Reddy and agreed with its overruling of Naraini Devi v. Smt. Ramo Devi; it also relied on the principle in Eramma v. Veerupanna and Mangal Singh v. Shrimati Rattno that enlargement requires some existing ownership interest.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_transfer and property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance and preexisting_maintenance_right and female_holds_limited_ownership

predicates.appeal_challenging_transfer: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree that invalidated a transfer by a female holder.
predicates.property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance: A female holder acquired property in place of maintenance or arrears of maintenance.
predicates.preexisting_maintenance_right: The property was given in recognition of a maintenance right that existed before the grant.
predicates.female_holds_limited_ownership: The female holder possessed the property with an existing ownership interest that was restricted in some respects.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenging a transfer concerns property given to a female holder in place of maintenance in recognition of her pre-existing right, and she held a limited ownership interest in it, that interest enlarges into full ownership.

issues.legal_issue: A female holder has limited ownership of property when she has its possession, control, and enjoyment for life to the exclusion of others, even if she cannot alienate it and others are also barred from dealing with it.
material_facts: The decree entitled the widow to take possession of the land after maintenance default and to enjoy its income for her lifetime.
The decree prohibited the widow from transferring the land and also deprived the other holders of the right to alienate it during her lifetime.
After the widow took possession, the other holders could not deal with the land to her detriment, and she could challenge their acts.
issues.conclusion: The widow held the land as a limited owner; her interest therefore enlarged into full ownership, and her transfer was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) applies where a Hindu female possesses property as a limited owner; it does not create ownership for a mere trespasser without any vestige of title. Limited ownership includes beneficial possession, control, and usufruct to the exclusion of others, although the holder's power of alienation is restricted. The Court applied Eramma v. Veerupanna, Mangal Singh v. Shrimati Rattno, and V. Tulasamma v. V. Sesha Reddy.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_transfer and female_has_exclusive_lifetime_control and female_has_restricted_alienation_power and others_cannot_deal_with_property

predicates.appeal_challenging_transfer: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree that invalidated a transfer by a female holder.
predicates.female_has_exclusive_lifetime_control: A female holder possesses and enjoys property for her lifetime, with control over it to the exclusion of others.
predicates.female_has_restricted_alienation_power: The instrument or arrangement restricts the female holder from transferring the property.
predicates.others_cannot_deal_with_property: Other persons are also barred from dealing with the property during the female holder's lifetime and cannot act to her detriment.

issues.definition: If, in an appeal challenging a transfer, a female holder has exclusive control and enjoyment of property for life, her power to alienate is restricted, and others cannot deal with the property, she holds full dispositive ownership.
